dek.en: Members start being named in #role-announcements, Optimum ships a game that races mump2p, gathers coding researchers at MIT, and puts a number on what speed is worth.

en: This register begins here. On 6 March BlockchainJeff posted the first role call in #role-announcements: six members promoted to Refined. Three more followed by the end of the month, and from the fourth on, Flash took over the weekly post.

The company had a big month too. It shipped a small game that dares you to beat mump2p, held the DeCo workshop at MIT, and published its first estimate of what faster propagation is worth in staking revenue: about 0.6 to 0.7% more for every 50 ms of usable slot time.
Four role calls named 45 members Refined: on 6, 17 and 23 March by BlockchainJeff, and on 30 March by Flash. The 23 March list credited the Mumbassadors with the selection.
Growth manager abbas_tfu built Are you faster than mump2p?, an aim trainer whose targets appear at mump2p’s block speed. DeCo brought coding researchers to MIT on 23 and 24 March.
A study by Optimum’s researchers estimated about 0.6 to 0.7% more validator revenue per 50 ms of extra slot time, and 13 to 16% higher MEV bids for 50 to 150 ms.

body.en: On 6 March BlockchainJeff posted the first role call in #role-announcements, naming six members Refined. Eleven followed on 17 March and eighteen on 23 March, a list described as selected by the Mumbassadors for activity, support and overall contribution. On 30 March Flash posted ten more, and has posted the role calls ever since. Every one of the 45 names is listed below and has a page on this register.

On 5 March Optimum released a browser game built by its growth manager abbas_tfu: an aim trainer at game.gmum.cc whose targets appear at the same speed mump2p delivers blocks across Ethereum. Players posted scores, and a day later Optimum admitted the launch had been a humbling experience. It was the first game from the team itself, half a year after the community’s Opti Runner.

On 26 March Moritz Grundei, Slobodan Sudaric-Hefner, Sajida Zouarhi and Muriel Médard published an estimate of how faster propagation pays. From Xatu and Rated data, each extra 50 ms of usable slot time matched about 0.6 to 0.7% more average revenue for the largest operators. A week of relay data suggested 50 to 150 ms more time would lift average MEV bids by 13 to 16%, and head vote accuracy could rise from about 98.6% to between 98.8 and 99.1%. The authors note the figures are correlations, not a controlled test.

On 23 and 24 March Optimum held DeCo, its first workshop on decentralized coding, at MIT, after Médard hosted a prep session the Sunday before. Speakers included Lara Dolecek of UCLA, Sreeram Kannan of EigenCloud, Guillermo Angeris of Bain Capital Crypto, Viveck Cadambe of Georgia Tech and Aditi Partap of Stanford, alongside Optimum’s own researchers. Optimum had opened it to 30 to 50 builders, researchers and academics.

Kent Lin spoke to Blockwind on 3 March, Médard laid out Optimum’s chain acceleration thesis on the BlockHash podcast on 5 March, and CryptoCoinShow published a follow up article on 9 March. On 25 March Médard joined The Rollup’s livestream from the Digital Asset Summit in New York, and Optimum offered to help the largest new staking operation improve its validators. On YouTube Médard and Moritz Grundei compared Reed Solomon with RLNC in a 39 minute session.

sources: Optimum on X, Kent Lin on Blockwind

body.en: On 16 March Optimum announced its EthCC plans: co-sponsoring the Blockspace Forum on 31 March, an event about how transactions move from user to block, and a talk by chief product officer Sajida Zouarhi on the cost of tail latency in Ethereum’s proposer builder pipeline, which she gave on 2 April.
